docs.title: VozLab
docs.text:
Local, private voice dictation for Windows. Hold a key, speak, release — your words appear in whatever app you're using, formatted. Speech recognition and text cleanup run on your own machine. No cloud, no subscription, no account, and no audio leaving your network.

  • :material-microsoft-windows: Install the app — 2 minutes, no admin rights, works with Smart App Control enabled.

  • :material-server: Set up the server — one command on any machine with Docker.

  • :material-shield-lock: How private is it? — everything VozLab stores and sends, plus how to verify it yourself.

  • :material-speedometer: Models & speed — pick a model for your hardware.

docs.title: The 30-second version
docs.text:
your laptop (Windows)                      your server (Docker, on your LAN)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────┐      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  hold right Ctrl ──► record mic  │      │  Whisper  speech → text (GPU or CPU)       │
 │        │                         │      │      │                                     │
 │        └── POST /transcribe ─────┼─────►│      ▼                                     │
 │            (WAV + token)         │      │  local LLM  cleanup (fillers, punctuation) │
 │                                  │      │      │  guard: never invents words        │
 │  paste into the focused app ◄────┼──────┤      ▼                                     │
 └──────────────────────────────────┘      └────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Typical wait: under a second on a GPU (0.5–0.9 s for a six-second sentence), a few seconds on CPU only.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 🎙️ Dictation into any Windows app, hold-to-talk or toggle, optional auto-stop
  • ✨ Local AI cleanup: filler words removed, punctuation and capitalisation fixed, your language preserved (English and Spanish tested)
  • 🌍 Multilingual with automatic detection (90+ languages)
  • 🔒 Zero telemetry, no audio on disk, nothing logged unless you ask
  • 🐳 Server runs on NVIDIA GPU, CPU-only, NAS or Raspberry Pi
  • 📋 Clipboard-safe pasting, dark UI, first-run wizard, one-command updates

Full feature list and screenshots: the repository README.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
Base URL: http://<server-ip>:8092 · API version: 1 (see /version).

All endpoints except /health and /version require the bearer token that the server generates on first boot:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Cheap liveness probe. No authentication, no secrets — safe for a monitoring tool.

{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "api": 1,
  "whisper_model": "small",
  "language": "auto",
  "cleanup": true,
  "cleanup_model": "qwen2.5:7b-instruct",
  "device": "cuda"
}

device is cuda when a GPU was found, otherwise cpu.

docs.title: GET /version
docs.text:
{ "name": "vozlab", "version": "1.2.0", "api": 1 }

The client compares version with its own and warns when major.minor differ, so users know to update the other half.

docs.title: POST /transcribe
docs.text:
The only real endpoint: audio in, text out.

Body raw audio bytes (WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC — anything PyAV can decode) Query cleanup=true\|false (default: server setting) Query language=en\|es\|auto… (default: server setting) Header Authorization: Bearer <token> Header Content-Type: audio/wav Limit 25 MB per request 
curl -X POST "http://192.168.0.23:8092/transcribe?cleanup=true" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: audio/wav" \
     --data-binary @recording.wav

{
  "text": "Meeting moved to Monday.",
  "raw_text": "um the meeting is moved to monday",
  "cleanup_used": true,
  "cleanup_rejected": null,
  "language": "en",
  "timings": { "whisper_s": 0.41, "cleanup_s": 0.26, "total_s": 0.69 }
}
  • text — what the client pastes. Equals raw_text when cleanup is off, failed, or was rejected by the guard.
  • cleanup_rejected — null, or the reason the cleaned text was discarded (for example invented 8 words (>2): ['yes', 'i', 'am']). Useful in logs.
  • language — the language Whisper detected or the one you forced.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Meaning What the client does 400 empty body reports "nothing was recognized" 401 missing/incorrect token tells the user to copy the token again 413 audio over 25 MB reports the recording was too long 422 decoding/transcription failed surfaces the message, keeps running

docs.title: Server settings
docs.text: Right now the server reads data/config.json (or VOZLAB_* environment variables) at startup — the planned GET/PATCH /settings API will let the app change models and language without SSH.

docs.title: Example: fully scripted setup
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml -f docker-compose.full.gpu.yml up -d
TOKEN=$(docker logs vozlab 2>&1 | grep -A1 'TOKEN' | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8092/health

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
VozLab is two programs that talk over your LAN: a Windows tray app and a Docker server. Nothing is centralised, nothing phones home.

┌──────────────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ client/  (Windows, Python)   │        │ server/  (Docker, FastAPI)                │
│                              │        │                                           │
│ tray.py        tray icon     │        │ server.py   HTTP API + model lifecycle    │
│ hotkeys.py     global hook   │        │ cleanup.py  LLM prompt + safety guard     │
│ audio.py       mic capture   │  HTTP  │ Dockerfile  Python 3.12 + CUDA libs       │
│ api.py         HTTP client   │ ──────►│                                           │
│ ui/            windows, pill │ token  │ faster-whisper → CTranslate2 (GPU/CPU)    │
│ app.py         orchestration │        │ Ollama (sibling or host) → cleanup LLM    │
└──────────────────────────────┘        └───────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Hotkey — hotkeys.py installs one keyboard.hook and pushes events onto a queue. A worker thread does the real work, because Windows silently removes low-level hooks whose callback takes longer than ~300 ms.
  2. Recording — audio.py opens a 16 kHz mono float32 stream via PortAudio, tracks RMS (drives the pill's level meter) and optionally auto-stops after silence_ms of quiet following speech.
  3. Upload — api.py packs the frames into 16-bit PCM WAV in memory and posts them to /transcribe with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Recordings shorter than min_seconds are dropped before the request.
  4. Server — FastAPI writes the bytes to a temporary file (faster-whisper needs a path), runs Silero VAD to trim silence, transcribes, then deletes it.
  5. Cleanup — the transcript goes to the local LLM with a formatter prompt. cleanup.py:cleanup_ok() then checks the result and rejects any rewrite that invents words, falling back to the raw transcript.
  6. Insert — the client copies the text to the clipboard, sends Ctrl+V, and restores the previous clipboard a second later.

docs.title: Design decisions worth knowing
docs.text:
GPU is opt-in in Compose. Docker Compose merges deploy.resources… reservations.devices and cannot remove entries in an overlay, so a GPU request in the base file would break every CPU-only machine. Instead the base stacks request nothing and docker-compose.gpu.yml adds the GPU.

The cleanup guard exists because models misbehave. An instruct model will happily answer a dictated question ("are you responding to me?" → "Yes, I am responding to you."). The prompt forbids it, and the guard is the safety net.

Everything the app needs is in %APPDATA%\VozLab. The install directory holds only code, so updates never touch settings.

Hotkeys are matched by hardware scan code (e.g. right Ctrl = 285) with localised-name fallbacks, because the keyboard library reports key names in the OS language ("ctrl derecha" on Spanish Windows).

The client is a package, not a script. run_vozlab.py is a thin dev entry point; PyInstaller builds the same code into the tray app. The headless UI renderer (client/tools/ui_preview.py) runs every window with demo data, which is how the screenshots and the demo GIF are generated.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
Artifact Built by For whom VozLab-<v>-src.zip + deploy.ps1 CI on tag everyone (SAC-safe) VozLab-Setup-<v>.exe Inno Setup on CI users with Smart App Control off VozLab-<v>-portable.zip PyInstaller on CI no-install portable runs ghcr.io/…/vozlab-server:<tag> Docker buildx on CI server operators SHA256SUMS CI verifying downloads

Each release also publishes checksums; deploy.ps1 verifies them before installing.

docs.title: Automatically (GitHub Actions)
docs.text:
1. Bump VERSION in client/vozlab/__init__.py and server/server.py, and add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
  2. Commit, then tag and push:
git tag v1.1.1
git push origin v1.1.1
  1. The Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) builds on windows-latest:
  2. runs the test suite,
  3. builds the app with PyInstaller,
  4. builds the installer with Inno Setup (installed via Chocolatey),
  5. creates a portable .zip,
  6. publishes a GitHub Release with both artifacts.

The workflow fails fast if the tag doesn't match VERSION in the code.

docs.title: Locally on Windows
docs.text:
cd client
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest tests -q
python run_vozlab.py            # run from source (dev mode)
pyinstaller vozlab.spec --noconfirm
# -> dist\VozLab\VozLab.exe

Then the installer (requires Inno Setup 6):

cd ..\installer
& "C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe" /DAppVersion=1.0.1 vozlab.iss
# -> installer\output\VozLab-Setup-1.0.1.exe

docs.title: Locally on Linux/macOS (for testing, not for shipping)
docs.text:
The app is Windows-targeted, but the code runs elsewhere for development:

cd client
sudo apt-get install -y libportaudio2      # PortAudio for sounddevice
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest tests -q
pyinstaller vozlab.spec --noconfirm        # produces a Linux binary

docs.title: Code signing
docs.text:
Unsigned builds trigger SmartScreen ("More info → Run anyway" — harmless) and are blocked outright by Smart App Control (no bypass, by design). Signing is therefore required to distribute to other people; self-signed certificates do not satisfy Smart App Control (it only trusts CA-issued chains).

Option Cost Notes Azure Trusted Signing ~$10/month Microsoft-trusted, no hardware token, made for CI. Best fit for this repo: add azure/trusted-signing-action to release.yml. Identity validation required (individual validation needs verifiable history). OV certificate (DigiCert/Sectigo…) ~$200–400/year Needs a cloud HSM (Azure Key Vault) or hardware token for CI. SmartScreen reputation builds up over downloads. EV certificate ~$300–500/year Immediate SmartScreen trust; hardware token or cloud HSM.

CI sketch (Trusted Signing) — sign both the app and the installer, in order:

      - uses: azure/trusted-signing-action@v0
        with:
          endpoint: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TS_ENDPOINT }}
          trusted-signing-account-name: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TS_ACCOUNT }}
          certificate-profile-name: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TS_PROFILE }}
          files-folder: client/dist/VozLab
          files-folder-filter: exe,dll
      # then build the installer so it wraps the signed binaries,
      # and sign installer/output/VozLab-Setup-*.exe the same way

Until then: Windows users with Smart App Control enabled should run from source.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to VozLab are documented here. This project follows Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: [1.2.0] — 2026-10-13
docs.text: A release aimed at strangers on the internet: installable without code signing, documented end to end.

docs.title: Added — distribution
docs.text:
• installer/deploy.ps1: one-click installer that works with Smart App Control enabled. Downloads the release source, verifies its SHA256 against SHA256SUMS, builds a private virtual environment and launches the app with the signed pythonw.exe. Plus VozLab.bat (double-click) and update.ps1 (in-place updates that keep your settings).
  • Release workflow now publishes VozLab-<v>-src.zip and SHA256SUMS, and builds
  • pushes ghcr.io/<owner>/vozlab-server:<tag|latest> so the server needs no local build.
  • docker-compose.full.yml: all-in-one stack (server + Ollama + model preload).
  • install.sh --with-ai / --cpu / --help with preflight checks.

docs.title: Added — client
docs.text:
• updater.py and in-app update flow: Check now, Update now (runs the updater), and an opt-in automatic check. Off by default — zero telemetry.
  • diagnostics.py + Settings → System → Export diagnostics: a support report with the token and every dictated word removed, plus Report a problem and Documentation buttons.
  • Server/client version-mismatch warning with upgrade instructions.

docs.title: Added — documentation
docs.text:
• Complete README rewrite (two-track quick start, screenshots, latency tables, privacy, FAQ, roadmap) and a Spanish mirror (README.es.md).
  • New guides: ARCHITECTURE, API, CONFIGURATION, MODELS, PRIVACY, REMOTE, FAQ, plus CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, issue and PR templates.
  • Docs site (MkDocs Material) with a GitHub Pages workflow.
  • Animated demo GIF generated from the real UI, and regenerated screenshots.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• GPU support is opt-in in Compose (.gpu.yml overlays) because Compose cannot remove device reservations in an override — CPU-only machines now start cleanly on the base files.
  • Default cleanup model is qwen2.5:7b-instruct (Apache-2.0) instead of llama3.1:8b (Meta licence): same 8/8 quality score and 0.25 s latency in the benchmark, better Spanish punctuation, friendlier licence for redistribution.
  • The cleanup guard is now accent-insensitive, so restoring accents in Spanish ("que tal" → "¿qué tal?") is no longer mistaken for inventing words.
  • /version and /health expose api: 1; VOZLAB_* environment variables can override any server setting.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Spanish text is no longer rejected by the cleanup guard when the model adds accents.
  • deploy.ps1-installed apps are updated in place instead of being duplicated.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Sound feedback is now off by default. No more beeps out of the box; turn it on any time in Settings → System → Sound feedback. Existing configs are migrated once (a config_version field) so installed copies go quiet too, unless you had explicitly enabled it.
  • Settings: the switch now has a short description.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Complete UI redesign (CustomTkinter): dark, modern interface throughout
  • animated status pill with a live microphone level meter and pulsing "transcribing" indicator, real rounded corners and fade in/out
  • settings window rebuilt as grouped cards (Connection, Dictation, Local AI formatting, Appearance, System) with a live connection indicator, toggle switches, segmented controls and a key-cap style hotkey display
  • first-run wizard with progress dots, step titles and an in-line microphone test that shows the live level while recording
  • styled About window
  • UI preview tool (client/tools/ui_preview.py) to render every window with demo data — works headless (Xvfb) for screenshots and development on Linux
  • Screenshots in docs/images/ (English + Spanish)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Requires customtkinter; PyInstaller spec collects its theme assets
  • Spanish and English strings for all new UI text

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The AI formatting pass could "answer" dictated questions. Saying "are you responding to me?" produced "Yes, I am responding to you." because the cleanup model treated the transcript as a conversation. The cleanup prompt now forbids replying (with question examples), and a new server-side guard rejects any rewrite that invents words, falling back to the raw transcript.
  • Whisper: condition_on_previous_text=False for dictation clips (reduces invented text on short/quiet audio).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Server: cleanup_guard setting, cleanup_rejected field in /transcribe responses, and a test suite for the cleanup prompt + guard (15 tests).
  • Client: dictations are logged with both the raw and the formatted text (%APPDATA%\VozLab\vozlab.log), and rejections are reported in the log.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Dictation always failed with "recording too short": the recorder cleared its audio buffer before the app asked how long the recording was, so every clip measured 0 s and was discarded. The finished recording's duration is now remembered on stop. (Regression tests added.)
  • CI: bumped actions/checkout and actions/setup-python to versions that no longer run on the deprecated Node 20 runtime.

docs.title: [1.0.0] — 2026-10-13
docs.text: First public release.

docs.title: Client (Windows)
docs.text:
• System tray application with state-aware icon (idle / listening / transcribing / offline)
  • Floating status pill showing live state and a preview of the transcribed text
  • First-run wizard: server connection test, dictation-key calibration, microphone test
  • Push-to-talk and toggle modes; optional auto-stop on silence
  • Hotkey matching by hardware scan code (works on any keyboard layout/language) with localized-name fallbacks
  • Clipboard-safe pasting (restores your previous clipboard)
  • Settings window (EN/ES) with start-with-Windows support
  • File logging to %APPDATA%\VozLab\vozlab.log

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
• FastAPI service with /transcribe, /health, /version
  • faster-whisper (CTranslate2) with CUDA auto-detection and CPU fallback
  • Multilingual: small model + automatic language detection, per-request language override
  • Optional LLM cleanup pass via Ollama (llama3.1:8b by default), language-preserving prompt
  • Zero-config first boot: token generated automatically and printed in the logs
  • 25 MB request cap, bearer-token auth, GPU/CPU compose files, one-command install.sh

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text:
• PyInstaller spec, Inno Setup installer (per-user, no admin prompt)
  • GitHub Actions: tests on Linux + Windows, tag-driven release build

docs.title: Windows app
docs.text: The VozLab app lives in your tray and turns your microphone into text in any application: hold a key, speak, release.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Download VozLab-Setup-x.y.z.exe from the repository's Releases page.
  2. Run it. It installs per-user (no administrator prompt) to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\VozLab.
  3. Optional: tick Start VozLab automatically when I sign in.

Windows SmartScreen will warn about an unknown publisher on first run (the app is not code-signed): More info → Run anyway.

docs.title: First-run wizard
docs.text:
1. Server — paste the URL and token your server printed (e.g. http://192.168.0.23:8092), then Test connection. A green "Connected! Model: small on cuda" means you're done here.
  2. Dictation key — press the key you want to use (e.g. right Ctrl). The app stores the key's hardware code, so it keeps working if you change Windows display language or keyboard layout.
  3. Microphone — record 3 seconds and see the transcription. If it's empty, check Windows Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone.

Click Finish — the app minimises to the tray and starts listening.

docs.title: Daily use
docs.text:
Action How Dictate Hold your key, speak, release (default mode) Dictate (toggle mode) Press the key to start, press again to stop Cancel a recording Press Esc… or just stay silent (auto-stop, if enabled) Open settings Tray icon → Settings… Change the key Tray icon → Change dictation key… Quit Tray icon → Quit

The floating pill shows Listening… while recording, Transcribing… while the server works, then a short preview of your text.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Notes Server URL / Token where your server lives; use Test connection Dictation key any key, including media keys you never use Dictation mode hold-to-talk, or press-to-start/stop Stop automatically when I stop speaking hands-free: press once, talk, it stops itself Format text with the local AI off = raw Whisper output (fastest) Dictation language auto-detect, or force en, es, … Interface language auto (follows Windows), English, Spanish Sound feedback off by default; short beeps when recording starts/stops Restore clipboard after pasting your previous clipboard comes back Show floating status pill hide it if you prefer silence Start with Windows autostart at login Debug logging verbose log in %APPDATA%\VozLab\vozlab.log

Settings are stored in %APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json; the log sits next to it (tray → Open settings folder).

docs.title: How the app behaves with other software
docs.text:
• Global hotkey works in Notepad, browsers, editors, chat apps, Office, etc.
  • Exclusive full-screen games that read the keyboard directly will not deliver the hotkey; use a toggle-mode hotkey or Dictate (toggle) from the tray.
  • The app pastes with Ctrl+V. In apps where Ctrl+V is remapped, text may not land — turn off Restore clipboard after pasting if the paste gets mangled.
  • Windows can block global hooks for processes running as a different user. If the hotkey does nothing, try launching VozLab as administrator once.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text: Install a newer VozLab-Setup-x.y.z.exe over the old version — settings and logs are preserved (they live in %APPDATA%\VozLab, not in the install folder).

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text: Windows Settings → Apps → VozLab → Uninstall (or the Start-menu uninstaller). Your settings file is left behind; delete %APPDATA%\VozLab if you want it gone.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text: Two configuration files exist: one for the app (your laptop) and one for the server (the machine with Docker). Neither needs editing by hand — the app's settings window and install.sh cover almost everything.

docs.title: Client — %APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json
docs.text:
Everything here is editable from the tray icon → Settings. The file is shown for completeness and for advanced tweaks; the app rewrites it on save.

Key Default Meaning server_host — server IP or hostname (192.168.0.23) server_port 8092 server port token — the token printed by the server hotkey — hardware scan code (e.g. 285 = right Ctrl) or key name hotkey_mode "hold" hold (push-to-talk) or toggle auto_stop false end the recording automatically after you stop speaking silence_ms 1200 how long a pause ends an auto-stop recording silence_rms 0.012 audio level treated as silence min_seconds 0.4 recordings shorter than this are ignored max_seconds 60 hard limit per recording cleanup true ask the server to run the AI formatting pass language "auto" language hint (auto, en, es, …) beeps false short beeps when recording starts/stops restore_clipboard true put your previous clipboard back after pasting ui_language "auto" interface language (auto follows Windows) show_pill true show the floating status pill pill_position "bottom-center" bottom-center, bottom-right, top-right launch_at_login false start with Windows check_updates false opt-in GitHub release check debug false verbose log, including the text you dictate config_version — internal; drives settings migrations

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
%APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json     your settings
%APPDATA%\VozLab\vozlab.log      log (transcripts only with debug on)
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\VozLab\  the app + its virtual environment

Deleting config.json re-runs the first-run wizard. Deleting the whole %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\VozLab folder is a clean uninstall.

docs.title: Server — server/data/config.json
docs.text:
Created on first boot with a generated token. Edit it and restart (docker compose restart) — or use environment variables.

Key Default Meaning token generated shared secret; every request must present it whisper_model small tiny/base/small/medium/large-v3, add .en for English-only language auto auto-detect, or force en, es, … compute_type int8_float16 GPU quantisation (int8 on CPU) beam_size 5 higher = slightly more accurate, slower cleanup true run the LLM formatting pass cleanup_guard true reject AI rewrites that invent words cleanup_model qwen2.5:7b-instruct any Ollama model cleanup_base_url http://host.docker.internal:11434 where the cleanup LLM lives cleanup_temperature 0.0 keep at 0 for deterministic formatting cleanup_max_tokens 500 cap on the formatted output length

docs.title: Environment variables (Docker-friendly)
docs.text:
Set these instead of (or to override) the file — anything set here wins:

VOZLAB_TOKEN=…                  # pin the token
VOZLAB_WHISPER_MODEL=medium
VOZLAB_LANGUAGE=es
VOZLAB_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
VOZLAB_CLEANUP=true
VOZLAB_CLEANUP_GUARD=true
VOZLAB_CLEANUP_MODEL=qwen2.5:3b-instruct
VOZLAB_CLEANUP_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434
VOZLAB_CONFIG=/data/config.json # where to read/write the file

Example — pin tokens and models in Compose:

services:
  vozlab:
    image: ghcr.io/diegosanchezguijarro-creator/vozlab-server:latest
    environment:
      - VOZLAB_TOKEN=choose-something-long
      - VOZLAB_WHISPER_MODEL=small.en
      - VOZLAB_CLEANUP_MODEL=qwen2.5:3b-instruct

docs.title: Keeping the model resident
docs.text: The server preloads Whisper at startup and keeps the cleanup model in memory (keep_alive: -1), so the first dictation after a restart is as fast as the hundredth. Ollama's own OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE is not used by VozLab.

docs.title: CPU-only tuning
docs.text:
{
  "whisper_model": "small.en",
  "compute_type": "int8",
  "cleanup_model": "qwen2.5:3b-instruct"
}

Or switch cleanup off entirely ("cleanup": false) for the fastest possible path — you'll see filler words and looser punctuation.

docs.title: Contributing to VozLab
docs.text: Thanks for helping! Bug reports, docs fixes, translations and code are all welcome.

docs.title: Quick orientation
docs.text: I want to… Read run the server locally docs/SERVER.md run the client from source docs/BUILD.md understand the code layout docs/ARCHITECTURE.md add a translation below, "Translations" report a security issue SECURITY.md

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Client (any OS for development; Windows for the real thing):

cd client
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
python -m pytest tests -q          # 30 logic tests, no audio hardware needed
python run_vozlab.py               # run the tray app

Server:

cd server
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up -d --build
docker logs -f vozlab

Server tests (no Docker needed):

cd server && python -m pytest tests -q

docs.title: Previewing the UI without Windows
docs.text:
Every window renders with demo data, headless:

sudo apt-get install -y xvfb imagemagick
Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1440x900x24 &
cd client
DISPLAY=:99 python tools/ui_preview.py --lang es         # look at it
DISPLAY=:99 python tools/ui_preview.py --shot            # write docs/images/*.png
DISPLAY=:99 python tools/make_demo_gif.py                # regenerate demo.gif

docs.title: What CI checks
docs.text:
Every pull request runs on Linux and Windows:

  • byte-compilation of all modules,
  • pytest for the client (30 tests) and the server (17 tests),
  • compose-file validation (including "the base stacks never request a GPU"),
  • on tags: PyInstaller build, Inno Setup installer, source zip, checksums, and the GHCR server image.

Run the same things locally before pushing: python -m pytest tests -q in both client/ and server/.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text:
The UI is English/Spanish today and the strings live in one file: client/vozlab/i18n.py. To add a language:

  1. copy the "en" dictionary to a new key (e.g. "fr"),
  2. translate the values (keep {placeholders} intact),
  3. add the code to the language pickers in ui/settings_window.py (LANGUAGES and the UI-language CTkOptionMenu values),
  4. check parity: python -c "from vozlab import i18n; print(set(i18n.STRINGS['en']) ^ set(i18n.STRINGS['fr']))" should print an empty set.

client/tools/ui_preview.py --lang fr renders it for a screenshot.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• Keep the client dependency-light: customtkinter, sounddevice, numpy, keyboard, requests, pyperclip, pystray, pillow. Please ask before adding a new one.
  • Comment the why, not the what — especially around Windows quirks (hook timeouts, scan codes, Smart App Control).
  • No network calls outside your server. Anything that contacts the internet must be opt-in and documented in docs/PRIVACY.md.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
1. Fork, branch from main (feat/…, fix/…, docs/…).
  2. Keep the diff focused; update docs and CHANGELOG.md when behaviour changes.
  3. Make sure the test suites pass, and say in the description what you tested on real hardware (Windows version, GPU).
  4. If you changed a default, note it in the PR so it can be mentioned in the release notes.

docs.title: Good first issues
docs.text:
• Add a Spanish/other-language README tweak.
  • More model presets in docs/MODELS.md.
  • Extra dictation cases in server/tools/benchmark_cleanup.py.
  • Docs typos anywhere — small PRs are very welcome.

docs.title: Is it really free? Is there an account?
docs.text: Yes and no — no account, no subscription, MIT licence. Your only costs are the electricity of the machine running the server and (optionally) an NVIDIA GPU.

docs.title: Do I need a GPU?
docs.text: No. CPU-only runs roughly 5–10× slower: a six-second sentence takes a few seconds. Switch to whisper_model: small.en and cleanup_model: qwen2.5:3b-instruct, or turn cleanup off, and a modern CPU feels usable.

docs.title: How is this different from Wispr Flow / Superwhisper / OS dictation?
docs.text:
• Nothing leaves your network. Cloud dictation apps send your voice to their servers; Windows Voice Access and macOS Dictation run locally but have no AI formatting pass and no custom vocabulary.
  • No word limits, no subscription. The server is yours.
  • It works offline once installed.

The trade-off: you have to run a small server, and the setup is one step longer than installing a cloud app.

docs.title: Does it work in other languages?
docs.text: Yes — the default small model is multilingual with automatic detection (90+ languages). Spanish and English are covered by tests and benchmarks. For English-only dictation small.en is faster and more accurate.

docs.title: Why did it type something I didn't say?
docs.text:
Two different causes, and the log tells them apart: open the log from the tray (Open settings folder → vozlab.log).

  • raw=… is wrong → Whisper mis-heard. Speak closer to the mic, check the input device, or move to a bigger model (medium).
  • raw=… is right but the final text isn't → the AI pass rewrote it. The server's guard rejects anything that invents words; if you see it happening, please open an issue with that log line.

docs.title: Can friends use it with my server?
docs.text: They can, but the intended model is everyone runs their own server — nothing points at your machine by default. Pointing several people at one server works (the API is stateless) but the single token is shared, and your GPU does all the work. For a group, run one server per household.

docs.title: Does the client work on macOS or Linux?
docs.text: Not officially yet. It's plain Python, so python run_vozlab.py runs on Linux/macOS for development, but text insertion uses Windows-specific behaviour (Ctrl+V, registry autostart). Linux/macOS support is on the roadmap.

docs.title: How do I uninstall it?
docs.text:
• Client: Settings → Apps → VozLab → Uninstall (installer builds), or delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\VozLab and %APPDATA%\VozLab (source installs), plus the Start-menu shortcut.
  • Server: docker compose down in server/, then delete the folder. Add --volumes if you used the all-in-one stack and want the model cache gone too.

docs.title: Can I use a cloud API instead of local models?
docs.text: You could — the server is a thin wrapper — but that defeats the purpose: your audio and text would leave your machine. VozLab will stay local-only by design.

docs.title: Is there a phone app?
docs.text: No. Dictation needs a real keyboard to paste into; phones have their own keyboard dictation. The server could be driven by any client that can POST audio, though.

docs.title: Why is the installer unsigned? Windows blocked it!
docs.text: Code signing costs money (a certificate plus identity validation), so VozLab ships a Smart-App-Control-safe installer instead: deploy.ps1 runs the app with your signed Python rather than an unsigned .exe. Use the one-liner from the README; it works even with SAC enabled.

docs.title: Where does the name come from?
docs.text: voz (voice) + lab — the little lab at home that does the listening.

docs.title: Something else?
docs.text: Open an issue or check Troubleshooting first — most questions are answered there.

docs.title: Models & performance
docs.text: VozLab uses two models: one for speech-to-text (Whisper, inside the server container) and one for text cleanup (any Ollama model).

docs.title: Speech recognition — Whisper
docs.text:
Model Size on disk VRAM (int8) Languages Notes tiny 75 MB ~0.3 GB multilingual fastest, noticeably worse base 145 MB ~0.4 GB multilingual okay for short commands small 490 MB ~0.5 GB multilingual default — good balance small.en 490 MB ~0.5 GB English only more accurate than small for English, same speed medium 1.5 GB ~1.4 GB multilingual clearly better; needs ~2 GB free VRAM large-v3 3.1 GB ~3 GB multilingual best; needs a 8 GB+ card alone

Rule of thumb: English-only dictation → small.en; several languages → small; accuracy over speed → medium.

Change it in server/data/config.json:

{ "whisper_model": "medium", "language": "auto" }

…or with an environment variable: VOZLAB_WHISPER_MODEL=medium.

Notes:

  • int8_float16 quantisation (the default on GPU) costs almost nothing in accuracy and halves memory.
  • A 6–8 GB GPU comfortably runs small or medium plus a 7B cleanup model.
  • Whisper models are MIT-licensed and downloaded from Hugging Face on first use.

docs.title: Text cleanup — Ollama models
docs.text:
Model Download VRAM Licence Notes qwen2.5:3b-instruct ~2 GB ~2.5 GB Apache-2.0 fastest; good on CPU qwen2.5:7b-instruct ~4.7 GB ~4.7 GB Apache-2.0 default — best balance, good Spanish punctuation llama3.1:8b ~4.9 GB ~5.3 GB Meta Llama licence similar quality, heavier, non-Apache licence gemma2:9b ~5.4 GB ~6 GB Gemma licence good, needs more VRAM 
docker exec vozlab-ollama ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct     # or any model
# then set "cleanup_model": "qwen2.5:3b-instruct" in server/data/config.json

Set "cleanup": false to skip the LLM entirely: raw transcripts, ~0.2 s faster, filler words kept.

docs.title: Benchmarking your own setup
docs.text:
python server/tools/benchmark_cleanup.py qwen2.5:7b-instruct llama3.1:8b

It unloads models first (two 7–8B models cannot share an 8 GB card), verifies the model actually landed on the GPU, and scores each model against real dictation cases — filler removal, question-vs-answer, Spanish accents, numeric formatting. Sample output from the reference machine (RTX 4060, 8 GB):

qwen2.5:7b-instruct          8/8  avg 0.25s  (GPU)
llama3.1:8b                  8/8  avg 0.25s  (GPU)

docs.title: Measured end-to-end latency
docs.text:
~6 seconds of speech, default models (small + qwen2.5:7b-instruct):

Hardware Whisper Cleanup Total RTX 4060 8 GB 0.2–0.6 s 0.25 s ~0.5–0.9 s RTX 3060 12 GB 0.3–0.7 s 0.3 s ~0.6–1.0 s GTX 1650 4 GB (small.en) 0.6–1.2 s 0.4 s ~1.0–1.6 s Ryzen 5 5600, CPU only 1.5–4 s 3–8 s ~5–12 s Raspberry Pi 5, CPU only 8–20 s — (cleanup: false) ~8–20 s

CPU timings improve a lot by switching to small.en + qwen2.5:3b-instruct, or by disabling cleanup.

docs.title: Memory footprint at runtime
docs.text: Reference machine (RTX 4060): small + qwen2.5:7b-instruct = 5.1 GB VRAM of 8.2 GB, leaving room for a browser. System RAM: the server container idles around 700 MB; the client around 60 MB.

docs.title: Privacy & security
docs.text: VozLab is designed so that your voice never leaves your network. This page documents exactly what happens to your data, and what you can verify yourself.

docs.title: What is collected
docs.text:
Nothing. No analytics, no crash reporting, no usage counters, no account, no device identifiers.

The app makes exactly two kinds of network request:

Request When Destination GET /health and POST /transcribe normal use your server, on your LAN GET /releases/latest only if you enable Settings → System → Check for updates, or press Check now api.github.com (public version number)

The second one is off by default. With it off, the only packets VozLab sends are to the IP address you typed in the wizard.

deploy.ps1 / update.ps1 also contact GitHub, but only when you run them, to download a release you asked for.

docs.title: What is stored
docs.text:
Where What Why server/data/config.json token, model settings server configuration (mode 600, git-ignored) server/data/hf/ Whisper model weights so startup doesn't re-download ~500 MB server/data/ + ollama_data/ LLM model weights (Docker volume) same %APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json server URL, token, your preferences so the app remembers everything %APPDATA%\VozLab\vozlab.log timestamps, state changes, errors support/debugging

Audio is never written to disk. It lives in memory on the client, and on the server the only disk touch is a temporary file inside the container that faster-whisper needs to read; it is deleted immediately after transcription. It is not a recording — no preview, no history, no retention policy to configure.

Transcripts reach vozlab.log only when Debug logging is on (it is off by default). Turn it off and clear the file from Settings → System → Open settings folder. To audit what a shared PC saw, delete that folder; nothing else is kept.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Every /transcribe request must send Authorization: Bearer <token>; anything else gets 401. The token is generated with secrets.token_urlsafe(24) on first boot and printed in the container log.
  • /health and /version are unauthenticated on purpose: they expose the model name, device and version number, nothing personal, and they make monitoring simple. Bind them to your LAN only.
  • Keep the server on a trusted LAN. The API is plain HTTP: anyone who can sniff your network AND has the token could send audio to it. If you need remote access, use a VPN (docs/REMOTE.md) rather than port-forwarding.
  • Rotating the token: edit server/data/config.json, restart the container, and update each client (Settings → Connection → token).

docs.title: Threat model (what VozLab does and does not protect against)
docs.text: Scenario Covered? Cloud provider reading your dictations ✅ impossible — there is no cloud A friend on your Wi-Fi seeing your audio ⚠️ partially — audio is unencrypted on the LAN; use a VPN or trusted network Someone with your laptop reading the token ❌ not yet — the token is stored in plain text (DPAPI storage is on the roadmap) Someone opening your server's port from the internet ⚠️ they still need the token, but do not expose it; use a VPN An LLM "helpfully" rewriting your text ✅ the guard rejects rewrites that invent words, falling back to the raw transcript Malicious model in Ollama ⚠️ model weights run as data, but Ollama is a separate process you control; pin models you trust Supply chain (pip/Docker) ⚠️ dependencies are version-pinned and scanned in CI (pip-audit, secret scanning); SBOM is on the roadmap

docs.title: Verifying the claims
docs.text:
1. Watch the traffic: run sudo tcpdump -i any -n 'not port 22' (or Wireshark) while dictating. You will see connections only to your server's IP:8092.
  2. Confirm no audio on disk: docker exec vozlab ls -la /tmp after a few dictations — nothing accumulates.
  3. Check the log contents: %APPDATA%\VozLab\vozlab.log with debug off contains state changes and errors, not your sentences.
  4. Read the code: the whole client is ~1500 lines of Python in client/vozlab, and the server is two files in server.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: Please open a private security advisory (repository → Security → Advisories) or email the maintainer rather than filing a public issue. We aim to respond within a few days. See SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Using VozLab away from home
docs.text: The server speaks plain HTTP and is meant for a trusted LAN. To dictate from a café, a hotel or your phone hotspot, put the connection inside a VPN instead of exposing port 8092 to the internet.

docs.title: Option 1 — Tailscale (easiest, free for personal use)
docs.text:
Tailscale gives every device a private IP (100.x.y.z) reachable from anywhere, with no port forwarding and no firewall changes.

# on the server
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up          # log in with the same account as the laptop
tailscale ip -4            # e.g. 100.101.102.103

Install the Tailscale client on the Windows laptop, log in with the same account, then in VozLab: Settings → Connection → Server URL = http://100.101.102.103:8092.

That's it — the dictation path now works over the tailnet, including from a phone hotspot.

docs.title: Option 2 — WireGuard (self-hosted)
docs.text:
If you prefer to run the VPN yourself:

sudo apt install wireguard
# generate keys, add a [Peer] for the laptop, then
sudo wg-quick up wg0

Point the client at the server's WireGuard address (usually 10.0.0.1).

docs.title: Option 3 — Public exposure (not recommended)
docs.text:
Only if you understand the trade-offs. Minimum requirements:

  1. TLS: put the API behind a reverse proxy with a certificate — Caddy does this in two lines: 
    voice.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8092
}
    Then set the client's Server URL to https://voice.example.com.
  2. A strong token (rotate it: edit server/data/config.json, restart, update clients).
  3. Firewall: allow only 443, and only the proxy should reach 8092.
  4. Monitoring: watch the logs for unexpected volume — docker logs -f vozlab.

Even then, remember that anyone who obtains the token can send audio to your server. A VPN avoids the whole question.

docs.title: Why the client can't "just" do HTTPS for you
docs.text: Certificate pinning (trust-on-first-use) is on the roadmap: it will let the Windows app talk to a self-signed HTTPS server without a browser-style certificate warning. Until then, use a VPN or a real certificate via Caddy.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: The latest release is supported. Please update (update.ps1 on the client, docker compose pull on the server) before reporting, since fixes ship there first.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text:
Please do not open a public issue for security problems.

  • Preferred: repository → Security → Advisories → Report a vulnerability (private, encrypted, keeps the discussion closed until fixed).
  • Or email the maintainer listed on the repository profile.

Include: what you did, what happened, what you expected, and the version numbers (vozlab.log has the client version; docker logs vozlab prints the server version at startup). A proof-of-concept helps enormously.

You can expect an acknowledgement within a few days, an assessment with a rough timeline, and credit in the release notes if you'd like it.

docs.title: Known design limits (not vulnerabilities)
docs.text:
These are documented, deliberate trade-offs — see docs/PRIVACY.md:

  • The API uses plain HTTP with a bearer token and is intended for a trusted LAN. Exposing port 8092 to the internet is not supported; use a VPN (docs/REMOTE.md).
  • The token is stored unencrypted in %APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json; anyone who can read your files can read the token. DPAPI storage is on the roadmap.
  • /health is unauthenticated and reveals the model name, device and version.
  • Audio is unencrypted on the LAN while in transit.

docs.title: Hardening checklist for operators
docs.text:
• Keep the server on a private network (or a VPN).
  • Rotate the token when a device is lost: edit server/data/config.json, docker compose restart, update the remaining clients.
  • Run the container as-is; don't add --privileged or mount the Docker socket.
  • Update the images regularly: docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.

docs.title: Server setup
docs.text: VozLab's server does the heavy lifting: speech recognition (Whisper) and the optional text cleanup (a local LLM). It runs in Docker on any machine on your LAN — a gaming PC, a home server, a NAS, a mini-PC.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Minimum Recommended OS Any Linux with Docker Engine 20.10+ Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 GPU none (CPU mode, ~5-10× slower) NVIDIA, ≥6 GB VRAM, driver ≥550 RAM 4 GB 8 GB+ Disk 3 GB (models + images) 6 GB

macOS/Windows servers are possible (Docker Desktop) but not tested.

docs.title: Easiest: published image + bundled AI
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/diegosanchezguijarro-creator/vozlab.git
cd vozlab/server
bash install.sh --with-ai

This pulls the published server image and Ollama, then downloads the cleanup model automatically (~4 GB, once). Nothing else to install.

docs.title: From this checkout (builds locally, uses an Ollama you already have)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/diegosanchezguijarro-creator/vozlab.git
cd vozlab/server
bash install.sh

install.sh detects a working NVIDIA GPU (adding the GPU overlay automatically) and falls back to CPU mode otherwise. It builds the image, starts the container and prints:

Server URL : http://192.168.0.23:8092
Token      : 3xKm9Qr2Lp8VtHzWnBc4YeSfUa1DgJ6o

First start downloads the Whisper model (~500 MB) into server/data/hf/.

docs.title: Manual install
docs.text:
cd server

# from this checkout (builds the image locally)
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up -d --build   # with NVIDIA GPU
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d --build                            # CPU only

# or use the published image + bundled Ollama (no build, needs no local Ollama)
docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml -f docker-compose.full.gpu.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml up -d                               # CPU only

docker logs -f vozlab                     # watch startup, shows the token

GPU support is opt-in (docker-compose.gpu.yml): the base stacks always run on CPU, so a machine without an NVIDIA GPU (or without the container toolkit) starts cleanly instead of failing on a device request.

docs.title: Connecting the app
docs.text:
1. Find the server's LAN IP: hostname -I (e.g. 192.168.0.23)
  2. In the VozLab app: Settings → Server URL = http://192.168.0.23:8092
  3. Token = the one printed in the logs / by install.sh
  4. Press Test connection — you should see the model and device.

docs.title: Settings — server/data/config.json
docs.text:
key default meaning token auto-generated shared secret required by every request whisper_model small small = multilingual, small.en = faster/English-only, medium = more accurate (needs ~5 GB VRAM) language auto detected per recording; set en, es… to force one compute_type int8_float16 GPU quantization; use int8 for CPU beam_size 5 higher = slightly more accurate, slower cleanup true LLM formatting pass (filler words, punctuation) cleanup_guard true reject LLM rewrites that invent words and keep the raw transcript cleanup_model llama3.1:8b any Ollama model or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint cleanup_base_url http://host.docker.internal:11434 where the cleanup LLM lives

Restart after editing: docker compose restart.

docs.title: The cleanup LLM (optional but recommended)
docs.text:
The cleanup pass is what makes dictation feel like writing instead of transcribing. VozLab talks to any OpenAI-compatible /api/chat endpoint — Ollama is the easiest:

curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
ollama pull llama3.1:8b

Smaller/faster alternatives: ollama pull llama3.2:3b then set "cleanup_model": "llama3.2:3b" (good for CPU-only servers).

Set "cleanup": false to skip the LLM entirely (fastest, raw transcripts).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
endpoint description GET /health status, model, device (no auth) GET /version {"name":"vozlab","version":"1.0.0"} POST /transcribe Authorization: Bearer <token>; raw audio body; ?cleanup=true|false, ?language=es

Example:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8092/transcribe \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     --data-binary @recording.wav

{"text": "Meeting moved to Monday.", "raw_text": "um the meeting is moved to monday",
 "cleanup_used": true, "language": "en",
 "timings": {"whisper_s": 0.4, "cleanup_s": 0.6, "total_s": 1.0}}

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
docker logs -f vozlab          # logs (shows the token at startup)
docker compose restart         # apply config changes
docker compose down            # stop
docker compose up -d --build   # update after a git pull

Backup/restore: server/data/ (config + model cache). Models re-download if lost.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• The API is HTTP with a bearer token — intended for a trusted LAN. Do not expose port 8092 to the internet. If you need remote access, use a VPN (WireGuard/Tailscale) rather than port-forwarding.
  • The token is the only credential; rotate it by editing config.json and restarting (docker compose restart), then update your clients.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Check the log first: tray icon → Open settings folder → vozlab.log. Enable Debug logging in Settings for per-keystroke detail.

docs.title: The hotkey does nothing
docs.text:
1. Make sure the app is running (tray icon present, blue mic).
  2. Re-run calibration: tray → Change dictation key…, press your key.
  3. Some apps (exclusive full-screen games, some remote-desktop sessions) swallow global hotkeys — try the tray menu → Dictate (toggle).
  4. If you run other automation tools, they may capture the key first; try another key (e.g. right Shift or F8).
  5. Run VozLab once as administrator to confirm it's a permissions issue.

Debug tip (development installs): this prints every key the hook sees —

python -c "import keyboard; keyboard.hook(lambda e: print(e.name, e.scan_code, e.event_type)); keyboard.wait()"

docs.title: "Cannot reach the server"
docs.text:
• Is the server running? On the server: docker ps and curl http://localhost:8092/health.
  • Same network? The client and server must be on the same LAN (no guest Wi-Fi isolation, no VPN split-tunnelling unless configured for it).
  • Correct IP? On the server: hostname -I. Then in the app: http://<that-ip>:8092.
  • Firewall on the server blocking 8092? sudo ufw allow 8092/tcp (or your distro's equivalent).
  • Docker not running on the server? sudo systemctl start docker.

docs.title: "The token was rejected" (401)
docs.text: Copy the token exactly as printed by install.sh / docker logs vozlab. Rotating the token server-side requires updating every client.

docs.title: Nothing is transcribed (empty result)
docs.text:
• Windows mic permission: Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone — allow desktop apps, and make sure the right input device is default.
  • Speak for at least ~0.4 s; trailing silence is trimmed.
  • Too quiet? Move closer or raise the input volume.
  • Check the app log for [dbg] lines and the server log for errors.

docs.title: Transcription is slow
docs.text:
• Check the server log line: loaded 'small' on cuda (fast) vs on cpu (slow).
  • CPU mode: expect 5–10× slower. Use small.en instead of small, or a smaller cleanup model (llama3.2:3b), or disable cleanup.
  • The first request after a restart is slower (models load). VozLab preloads Whisper at startup and keeps the cleanup model resident.

docs.title: Text pastes into the wrong place / doesn't paste
docs.text:
• The text goes wherever focus is when the paste happens. Click into your document right after releasing the key.
  • Apps that remap Ctrl+V may fail: disable Restore clipboard after pasting.
  • The app restores your clipboard ~1 s after pasting; if you copy something in that window, it can be overwritten — disable the option or paste manually.

docs.title: The status pill is missing / in the wrong place
docs.text: Settings → Show floating status pill. Position is controlled by pill_position in %APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json (bottom-center, bottom-right, top-right).

docs.title: The text isn't what I said
docs.text:
• Dictations are logged with both versions — open the log from the tray (Open settings folder → vozlab.log) and compare raw=... (what Whisper heard) with the final text (what the AI formatting produced).
  • If the raw text is wrong, it's an audio/accuracy problem: speak closer to the mic, and consider a bigger model (whisper_model: small.en for English-only is notably more accurate than the multilingual small; medium is better still).
  • If the raw text is right but the final isn't, the cleanup model rewrote it — the server's guard normally catches this and keeps the raw text (cleanup_rejected in the log). Send me that log line if it persists.
  • Turn off Format text with the local AI in Settings to check the raw output.

docs.title: Windows blocks the installer
docs.text:
Two different Windows features can do this:

SmartScreen — "Windows protected your PC". Click More info → Run anyway. Expected for unsigned software; harmless.

Smart App Control — "This app can't run because it's not signed" (Settings → Privacy & security → Windows Security → App & browser control → Smart App Control). There is no bypass — SAC only allows apps with a valid signature. Pick one:

  1. Run from source (recommended, keeps SAC enabled). Windows allows the app because it is launched by your signed pythonw.exe:
# in the repo's client folder (requires Python 3.11+)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\install_from_source.ps1

This creates a .venv, installs the dependencies, adds a VozLab Start-menu shortcut and launches the app. It behaves exactly like the installed build.

  1. Turn Smart App Control off — Settings → Privacy & security → Windows Security → App & browser control → Smart App Control → Off. ⚠️ Microsoft warns it can only be re-enabled by resetting Windows. Only do this if you are comfortable with that.

  2. Sign the build — required if you want to share the installer: every friend with SAC enabled would hit the same wall. See BUILD.md.

docs.title: vozlab container restarts in a loop (server)
docs.text:
• Check docker logs vozlab: usually a missing GPU (nvidia-smi not working) — use the CPU compose overlay, or fix the NVIDIA container toolkit.
  • Out of VRAM: switch whisper_model to small.en, or set cleanup: false.
  • Still stuck? docker compose down && docker compose up -d --build.

docs.title: Reset everything
docs.text:
Server: stop the container, edit server/data/config.json, start again (models are cached in server/data/hf/ and are only re-downloaded if deleted).

Client: delete %APPDATA%\VozLab\config.json — the setup wizard runs again on next start.
